title: Mutation Safety Envelope — Core Schema
description: Normative, domain-blind schema for MSE v0.1.0. This schema defines the safety envelope only. Domain-specific vocabulary (SKUs, fares, plans, billing periods, etc.) MUST NOT be added here — it belongs in a profile that extends `Effect.type` namespaces and `value` payloads. See /spec/normative-spec.md.

GuaranteeMode.description: Confidence classification for a predicted effect. EXACT: the value is guaranteed to hold at commit time if committed within validUntil. REVALIDATE: the value may drift and MUST be re-checked at or before commit. UNKNOWN: no guarantee is offered; the client MUST NOT rely on the value for acceptance-constraint evaluation.

validUntil.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Required when mode is EXACT or REVALIDATE if the guarantee is time-bounded. Absent validUntil with mode=EXACT means the guarantee does not expire before commit is attempted at all (implementations SHOULD still treat an unreasonably long-lived EXACT guarantee with suspicion; see security considerations).

type.description: Namespaced, domain-defined effect identifier in the form `<namespace>:<local_name>`, e.g. `retail:order_total_delta`. The MSE core assigns no meaning to any namespace or local_name; it only requires the shape. Profiles own the registry of meaningful values within their namespace.

value.description: Domain-defined payload for this effect. The core treats this as opaque. Profiles SHOULD constrain `value` to a specific, documented shape per effect type (e.g. a signed decimal amount + ISO 4217 currency code for a *_delta effect), but the core schema intentionally does not.

proposalId.description: Client- or server-generated identifier for this proposal, unique within the issuing system. MUST NOT be reused across distinct proposals.

target.description: Opaque, domain-defined reference to the existing commercial resource being mutated (e.g. an order id, itinerary id, subscription id). The core does not interpret this value.

change.description: Opaque, domain-defined description of the proposed mutation. The core does not interpret this value; it is passed through to the provider that produces a MutationQuote.

quoteId.description: Unique identifier for this quote. A commit request references this id.

target.description: Opaque reference to the resource this quote applies to. SHOULD match the `target` of the originating MutationProposal.

snapshot.description: Opaque, domain-defined reference or hash representing the state of `target` at quote time (e.g. a version, ETag, or content hash). Used by a provider to detect drift between quote and commit. Optional: not every provider can offer a snapshot reference.

effects.description: Predicted consequences of committing this quote. MAY be empty (a no-op or purely structural change), but the array key MUST be present.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp after which this quote MUST NOT be committed. A commit attempted after expiresAt MUST be refused by a conformant provider. If absent, the quote does not expire independently of its effects' own guarantee.validUntil values (the commit consistency rules in the normative spec still apply).

commitConsistency.description: Declares how a provider will use `snapshot` at commit time. SNAPSHOT_REQUIRED: commit MUST be refused if the resource's current state does not match snapshot. SNAPSHOT_ADVISORY: provider MAY warn or re-quote on drift but is not required to refuse. NONE: no snapshot-based drift detection is offered.

effectType.description: The Effect.type this constraint applies to.

value.description: Primitive comparable bound (number, string, or boolean). The core does not support comparing structured/object values; a profile that needs to compare structured effect values (e.g. currency-qualified amounts) MUST define and document its own comparison semantics for that effectType, and note this is a deliberate core limitation, not an oversight.

idempotencyKey.description: Opaque key supplied by the caller to allow safe retry of a commit request whose outcome is INDETERMINATE. MSE does not define the retry protocol itself (see 'What MSE does not define'); this field only reserves a place for one to be carried.

acceptanceConstraints.description: Bounds the caller requires to hold, checked against the final pre-commit quote. MAY be empty, meaning the caller accepts the quote unconditionally.

RefusalReason.description: Non-exhaustive, extensible in profiles via additional string values outside this enum is NOT permitted by this core schema version; profiles needing more reasons SHOULD map to PROVIDER_REJECTED and carry detail in an out-of-band/provider-specific field. This is flagged as an open ambiguity — see spec/normative-spec.md §Open Issues.

committedEffects.description: Present when outcome=APPLIED. The effects as actually realized at commit time, which MAY differ from the quoted effects only for effects whose guarantee.mode was REVALIDATE or UNKNOWN. A conformant provider MUST NOT silently alter an EXACT-guaranteed effect between quote and commit; doing so is a conformance violation, not a valid APPLIED result (see spec).

value.description: Domain-defined realized value for this effect, when known. MAY be absent when finality is PENDING or UNKNOWN.

settledAt.description: Timestamp at which finality became FINAL or FAILED. Absent while PENDING or UNKNOWN.

effectReceipts.description: Finality state for each effect the caller needs tracked. MAY be a subset of the quote's effects if others are not independently trackable; this is a known ambiguity (see spec).

description: This top-level schema is a container for the $defs above. MSE does not mandate a single wire envelope; implementations reference individual $defs (MutationProposal, MutationQuote, CommitRequest, CommitResult, Receipt) as needed for their transport.
